source: NaCCA Creative Arts Curriculum for Primary Schools (Basic 1–3), September 2019
accessibility: Prompts may be read aloud. Accept oral, written, drawing, movement or demonstration responses when appropriate. Assess the learning indicator, not personal identity or access to community visits. Use teacher-provided local examples; do not require learners to disclose private information.

indicators.statement: Think about people in the local community and describe their history, culture or way of life.
questions: Which can tell us about a community's history?
A story from a trusted elder
Name one part of a community's way of life.
Food, language, clothing, buildings, tools, songs or dances
What is a respectful question to ask a community elder?
A polite question about local history or culture
Name one kind of person who may share community history.
Elder, leader, parent, caregiver or knowledgeable community member
You are unsure whether a story is correct. What can you do?
Ask a teacher or check another reliable source
Draw a familiar community place or activity.
Drawing shows a relevant place or activity
Name one kind of building found in a community.
Home, school, market, clinic or palace
How can people learn about local culture respectfully?
Listen, observe and ask polite questions
What might traditional tools tell us?
Name one type of food people may share in a community.
A classmate describes a different custom. What is a kind response?
Listen and ask respectfully; do not mock
Which is a way to record what you learn?
Name one way people share their history.
Practise listening politely to a community story.
Why may communities have different customs?
People have different histories and traditions
Give one example of a community celebration or activity.
Tell or draw one fact about a community way of life using a provided example.
Why should we avoid making fun of another group's culture?
It shows respect for people and their heritage

indicators.statement: Think about and describe visual artworks produced or found in the local community.
questions: Name one visual artwork found in a community.
Pot, basket, poster, carving, drawing or textile
What can a clay pot be made from?
Name one material used to make an artwork.
Paper, clay, wood, fabric or safe found material
Match: poster; pot; basket to: shares a message; holds things; woven container.
Describe one artwork you have seen in a picture or in class.
Names or describes a relevant artwork
Draw a simple pattern you have seen on an artwork.
What might a poster be used for?
To share information or a message
You see an unfamiliar artwork. What can you do to learn about it?
Look carefully and ask a respectful question
Name one feature you can observe in an artwork.
Colour, shape, line, size or texture
What is a carving commonly made by shaping?
Why do people make useful artworks?
For a purpose such as holding, wearing or decorating
Tell one way a local artwork can show culture.
It may show patterns, symbols, materials or practices
A classmate's artwork looks different from yours. What is a good response?
Notice a feature kindly and respectfully
Which tool can make a drawing?
Match: line; colour; shape to what you can see in artwork.
Choose a pictured artwork and describe its material and use.
Gives one plausible material and use
Why should we handle displayed artworks carefully?

indicators.statement: Reflect on how local visual artworks reflect the natural environment.
questions: Which belongs to the natural environment?
Name one natural object an artist might observe.
Leaf, stone, flower, cloud or shell
Which feature can be noticed in a leaf?
Match: flower; stone; cloud with: soft petals; hard surface; changing shape.
Describe the colour or shape of a natural object.
What can an artist make from observing a tree?
Draw a natural object and show one feature.
A plant is growing in the school yard. How can you observe it safely?
Look without damaging or tasting it
Name one natural colour you might see outdoors.
How a surface feels or looks
How can natural objects inspire art?
Their colours, forms, patterns or textures give ideas
Which is a safe way to collect ideas from nature?
Draw or photograph without harming living things
A learner wants to pull flowers from a garden. Suggest a better choice.
Observe, draw or use fallen material with permission
Name one shape found in nature.
Round, oval, curved or another observed shape
Match: rough; smooth; shiny to a surface description.
Show a drawing inspired by a natural object and name its feature.
Why should we care for natural things?
They are part of our environment
Name one way nature can inspire a pattern.
Repeat shapes or lines seen in leaves, flowers or other forms

indicators.statement: Explore how local visual artworks reflect topical issues in the community.
questions: Which could be a community issue shown in an artwork?
Name one local issue an artwork could show.
Litter, flooding, road safety or a teacher-provided concern
What might a road-safety poster remind people to do?
What is a message in an artwork?
A drawing shows a blocked drain. What issue might it represent?
Poor waste disposal or flooding risk
How can a picture help people notice an issue?
Which material is suitable for a simple class poster?
Draw a picture encouraging people to keep a place clean.
Name one safe action to reduce litter.
Use a bin or carry rubbish until one is available
What should an artwork about a problem try to do?
A poster blames a person without evidence. How can it be improved?
Focus on the issue and helpful action, not accusation
What might a picture of children crossing carefully teach?
Match: blocked gutter; litter; unsafe crossing to possible concern.
Suggest one kind message for a clean-up poster.
Which is a helpful community message?
Name one visual feature that can make a message clear.
Colour, large shapes, simple picture or lettering
A learner has no local example. What can they use?
Explain a poster's helpful message to a classmate.
Make a simple sketch about a safe community action.
Sketch relates to a safe action
Why should community artworks avoid insulting people?

indicators.statement: Plan an imagined visual artwork reflecting local history and culture.
questions: What should you decide before making an artwork?
Name one way of life your artwork could represent.
A teacher-provided or learner-selected local custom
Which can help plan a picture?
A simple line showing the main shape
You want to show a local celebration. What could you plan first?
Choose a scene, shapes and materials
Sketch one idea for a culture-themed artwork.
Match plan step: idea; material; outline.
subject; what to use; first sketch
Name one material for a drawing.
It helps organise ideas before making
Tell what your planned artwork will show.
You do not know a cultural detail. What should you do?
Ask a teacher or use a provided source
Use verified details and avoid mockery
Name one local object that could inspire a picture.
A pot, basket, textile or building
Add one detail to show where or when the scene happens.
What can you change after looking at your sketch?
A plan can be changed when…
Describe the idea and material for a planned artwork.
Your first drawing does not show the idea clearly. What can help?
Add a detail or make a new outline
Name one way an artwork can show community identity.
Local pattern, object, clothing or place
Explain one choice you made in your plan.

indicators.statement: Develop ideas and choose tools, materials and methods for a visual artwork.
questions: Which tool is suitable for colouring a drawing?
Paper, pencil, crayon or clean reusable material
What can clay be used to make?
Name one tool used for drawing.
You plan to make a paper collage. What do you need?
Paper pieces and safe adhesive, with supervision
Match: pencil; crayon; clay to drawing; colouring; modelling.
Why should we choose materials before making?
So they suit the artwork idea
Name one way to make a pattern.
Repeat a line, shape or colour
Make a small outline for an artwork idea.
A tool is sharp or unfamiliar. What should you do?
Ask the teacher and use it only with permission
Which is a safe classroom practice?
Share tools carefully and follow instructions
Explain why a material suits your idea.
Shaping material to make a form
What can a basket be made by doing?
Match: cut paper; press clay; draw lines.
Name one way to reuse clean material in art.
Use clean boxes or paper scraps with permission
Your plan needs a colour you do not have. What can you do?
Choose another available colour or ask the teacher
Select a suitable tool and show how to hold it safely.
Why should tools be put away after art time?
To keep the room safe and tools ready
Name one choice you made about material or method.

indicators.statement: Explore tools, materials and methods for artworks reflecting natural and man-made environments.
questions: Which artwork method can show a leaf shape?
Name one safe reusable material for a model.
You want to show a park and a building. What could your artwork include?
Match: river; house; tree to natural or man-made.
Sketch one natural and one man-made object.
What can a pencil outline help you do?
Name one feature of a building.
Describe one way people change the environment.
Build, plant, farm or make roads
You collect a living plant for art. What is a better option?
Draw or observe it without removing it
Which surface might make an interesting texture rubbing?
What should you do before using collected materials?
Check with a teacher and ensure they are clean and safe
Match material to method: paper; clay; crayon.
Why show both natural and built features?
To represent the environment around people
Name one way to show a tree's texture or shape.
Make or describe a plan showing a natural and built feature.
Includes both and a suitable method
A material may be dirty or unsafe. What should you do?
Do not use it; ask the teacher
What is one benefit of planning before making?
The materials and idea fit together
Name one feature you could change to improve your outline.

indicators.statement: Choose tools, materials and methods for an artwork reflecting a local topical issue.
questions: Which art form can share a short public message?
Name a community issue a picture could show.
Litter, flooding, safe roads or teacher-provided issue
Which tool can make bold poster marks?
What should a poster message be?
You want to show clean water. What could you draw?
A clean stream and people protecting it
Match issue to message: litter; road safety; blocked drain.
use bin; cross carefully; keep drains clear
Sketch a simple poster idea about a safe action.
Why choose materials that suit your artwork?
Name one safe material for a poster.
Explain how your image communicates its message.
A poster uses too many small pictures. What might improve it?
Use a simpler, larger main image
Name one feature that makes a poster easy to understand.
Simple picture, readable words or strong contrast
You are not sure of a local issue's cause. What should you do?
Which is not a helpful message?
Match: paper; crayon; outline to poster surface; colour; planning.
Choose a material and describe a poster idea.
What should you do if a tool is not safe to use alone?
Ask for help and follow directions
Suggest a kind call-to-action for your poster.
How can an artwork help a community?
It can share ideas or encourage helpful action

indicators.statement: Create an imagined visual artwork reflecting local history or culture.
questions: Which can help create a picture of community life?
Name one form of visual artwork you can make.
Which tool can colour a picture?
What can a pattern be made from?
You are drawing a local celebration from a teacher-provided example. What detail could you include?
A verified object, place or activity
Create a simple pattern inspired by a local artwork.
Match: draw; doodle; model to picture; idea marks; three-dimensional form.
Name one useful artwork found in a community.
Stool, pot, basket or other suitable example
What should you do before using a tool?
Tell one idea your artwork shows.
The artwork is not as planned. What can you do?
Add, change or try another safe method
Use only what is needed and tidy up
Name one detail that can show a place.
Show a completed or partly completed artwork and identify its subject.
Why can art help tell a community story?
Images can show people, places and activities
Which material should be used only with permission and supervision?
Any unfamiliar or potentially unsafe tool/material
Match: colour; shape; line to visual features.
What can you do to make a drawing clearer?
Add important details or stronger outlines
A cultural detail is uncertain. How should you represent it?
Ask or use verified teacher-provided detail
Name one choice you made while creating.
Relevant tool, colour or subject choice

indicators.statement: Create visual artworks expressing ideas about natural and man-made environments.
questions: Name one man-made feature you can draw.
What can a repeated shape make?
Name a material for making a simple model.
Clean cardboard, paper or teacher-approved clay
Make a picture of a garden. Name one natural and one made feature.
Draw a natural object using lines or shapes.
Match: paper scraps; pencil; clay to collage; sketch; model.
What is one way to show a building's form?
Describe one difference between natural and man-made things.
Naturally occurring versus made by people
Which is a safe use of found material?
Use clean material approved by a teacher
You want to show a river without using real water. What can you use?
Blue lines or shapes on paper
Name one detail that helps show a tree.
Which tool is useful for an outline?
Make a small design including a natural and a built feature.
Why should we avoid damaging nature for art materials?
To care for living things and the environment
Match: smooth; rough; curved to a surface or line feature.
Your cardboard model is unstable. What could you change?
Adjust its base or joins with teacher guidance
An idea about a place or object
Name one choice that helped your artwork show its idea.
Relevant colour, shape, material or method
How can you care for tools after creating?
Clean, return and store them safely

indicators.statement: Create visual artworks expressing ideas about topical issues in the local community.
questions: Which could be shown in a community poster?
Name one safe action that can help a community.
Use bins, cross carefully or tell an adult about a hazard
Which picture might warn people about road safety?
A person crossing at a safe place
Name one material for a simple message picture.
You draw a blocked gutter. What helpful action could your picture suggest?
Keep drains clear or dispose of waste properly
Make a simple picture encouraging a helpful action.
Match: litter; unsafe crossing; dirty water to helpful action.
use a bin; cross safely; protect water
Explain the message in your artwork.
Everyone can help keep this place clean
Why use a clear main picture?
People can understand the message easily
Someone suggests drawing a dangerous action. What should you do?
Choose a safe alternative and ask the teacher
What can colour help an artist do?
Make parts of an image stand out
Name one local issue from a teacher-provided example.
Show a sketch and name the action it encourages.
Sketch relates to a safe action
What should you do if you are unsure about a fact in your artwork?
Check with the teacher or use a reliable provided source
Which is a responsible way to use art materials?
Use them safely and avoid waste
Match: large lettering; simple image; colour to readable words; clear idea; emphasis.
A classmate interprets your message differently. What might you improve?
Add a clearer image or words
Suggest one respectful slogan about safety.
How can art help people notice an issue?
It makes the issue and possible action visible
